clue.text: Contrast, after definite changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar point: a word for contrast, coming after an altered definite article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the thirteen letters of AFTER DEFINITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To differentiate between things is to set them against each other and mark the difference, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Son leaves Italian man with American — American numskull

indicators.note: the son leaves, so his letter is taken out of the Italian title

parts.note: Signor is the Italian form of address for a man
US, the United States, stands for American
US, the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A family story: a son walks out on an Italian man and an American, who is dismissed as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S out of SIGNOR, giving IGNOR; the two Americans then give AM and US.
explanation.definitionFit: A numskull is a dunce, and an ignoramus is a person lacking knowledge, so both are insults for a stupid person.

clue.text: Young Queen's boarded vessel

indicators.note: the Queen boards, getting on and so going inside the other word

parts.note: fry are young fish, so the young of a creature
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A youthful queen steps aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an adjective for the Queen, but it is a noun here: the young of fish are called fry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat carrying passengers across water, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Profligate outside can act

indicators.note: the profligate stands outside, wrapping round the word for can

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, profligate man
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A wastrel standing outside can still put on a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun, a tin container; 'act' is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a set performance, as in a comedian's act.

clue.text: Enthusiasts, about five hundred on island, all ready for take-off?

indicators.note: the enthusiasts go about, surrounding the following pieces

parts.note: nuts are fans or enthusiasts, as in golf nuts
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Fans gathered round about five hundred on an island, awaiting an aeroplane's departure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'take-off' as removing clothes, not a plane leaving; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go unclothed, so they are always prepared to strip everything off.

clue.text: One tyre nail's damaged as a matter of fact

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, stands for one

indicators.note: damaged tells us the letters of the tyre and nail words are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is no letter; the nail gives just its own word

explanation.surface: A single tyre has been damaged by a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' acts on just the tyre and nail words, giving NREALITY; 'One' stays outside the mix as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial expressions meaning actually, in truth.

clue.text: Hear socialist's gutted after meeting

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides, leaving just the outside letters of the word for socialist

explanation.surface: A socialist is devastated after hearing something at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties SOCIALIST, leaving ST; 'Hear' is the judge's sense, giving TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a meeting, especially a secret appointment between lovers.

clue.text: Walk on water

parts.note: not a miracle: a walk here is a place for strolling, and it is on a ship at sea

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a miracle, but 'Walk' is a noun, a promenade, found aboard a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the open upper level of a passenger ship where people stroll, so a walkway out on the sea.

clue.text: Performing on US comedian's pitches

parts.note: playing means performing, as on stage or an instrument
W C Fields was an American comedian of stage and film

explanation.surface: Someone performs at an American comedian's gigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sits between the pieces as a link. W C Fields was a US film comic of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitches are areas of ground marked out for sports such as football or cricket.

clue.text: Manage to get a cycle or small car

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a round is a cycle, as in a round of talks

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a bicycle or a little car to get around.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNAROUND is a British word for a small car used for short trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaround is a compact car kept for local errands, so a small motor vehicle.

clue.text: Return of play ordinarily featuring Prince, say

indicators.note: return means the letters are read backwards
featuring tells us the letters sit inside the words play ordinarily

explanation.surface: A commonplace revival of a stage play starring a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' shows LAYOR within 'pLAY ORdinarily'; 'Return of' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of a king's or queen's family, an example of the noun for such a person.

clue.text: Month in which bishop is to take a wife

indicators.note: in which places the bishop inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop chooses a particular month for his wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: RR, Right Reverend, is the form of address for a bishop, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to wed; a man taking a wife is getting wed.

clue.text: In filthy accommodation, housing worker left at once

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: housing means the sty holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a proverbially dirty dwelling
an ant is the crossword worker, after the worker ant

explanation.surface: A labourer living in squalid lodgings has walked out immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' in crosswords is very often an ant or a bee; here the insect lodges with L in the pig's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Instantly means immediately, without any delay.

clue.text: Person appointed in Nebraska to take care of old excavation

indicators.note: the state takes care of the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nebraska
a mine is a dug excavation

explanation.surface: Someone is given a job in Nebraska looking after an old dig.
explanation.walkthrough: US state abbreviations are fair game: Nebraska's postal code supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone named or proposed for a role or office.

clue.text: Mean behaviour from North-South, hampering East in playing Spades

indicators.note: the pair hampers, closing in around the anagram

parts.note: N and S are the compass abbreviations, a bridge partnership

indicators.note: playing tells us the letters of east and in are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A bridge table squabble: North-South obstruct East while spades are played.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting misleads: 'playing' mixes EAST IN into ASTINE, and 'from' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is spiteful, unkind conduct, which is what mean treatment of others is.

clue.text: Admitting row with boyfriend, nurse's become tougher

indicators.note: the nurse admits, letting the row in inside her letters

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is a British nursing grade
a tiff is a minor quarrel, the classic lovers' tiff

explanation.surface: A nurse who has quarrelled with her boyfriend has hardened.
explanation.walkthrough: An SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade; the lovers' quarrel is a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to grow firmer or more rigid, so to harden.

clue.text: Brother's left Arran, suspiciously

definitions.note: the possessive phrase is matched by an adjective meaning of or like a brother

indicators.note: suspiciously tells us the letters of left Arran are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brother has quit the Scottish island in suspicious circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges LEFT ARRAN. Arran is an island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal comes from Latin frater and describes what belongs to or befits a sibling of the male sex.

clue.text: Neglected daughter tagging along with heartless entertainer

indicators.note: the daughter tags along, coming after the other piece
heartless takes away the centre letter of the entertainer

parts.note: a diseuse is a female performer of monologues

explanation.surface: A girl was ignored while trailing after a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter of the performer's title, giving DISUSE; a diseuse recites monologues.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused is no longer used, so it has been abandoned or left untended.

clue.text: Vehicle bringing over Irish member taking in motoring organisation function

indicators.note: bringing over means the whole piece is turned round, read backwards
the member takes in, enclosing the next pieces

parts.note: TD, Teachta Dala, is a member of the Irish parliament
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation
to go is to function or work

explanation.surface: An Irish politician brings a car over and has the motoring club look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The container makes TRACGOD, and 'bringing over' turns it backwards. 'Irish member' means a member of the Dublin parliament, and the motoring club is a British breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogcart is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, once with a box for dogs.

clue.text: Player's careful taking drink

parts.note: fly means shrewd or wary, careful not to be caught out
a half is a half pint of beer

explanation.surface: A sportsman is cautious when it comes to drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A half is a British pub measure, half a pint. The fly-half is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-half is a rugby team member who plays between the scrum-half and the three-quarters.

clue.text: Motley group of men with guns welcomed by stage coach operator

indicators.note: the gunners are welcomed by, so taken inside, the operator

parts.note: Wells Fargo ran stagecoaches in the American West
the RA, Royal Artillery, are the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men are greeted by the company running a stagecoach line.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells Fargo is the stagecoach firm of Westerns; the RA, Royal Artillery, are the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble, so a motley assortment.

clue.text: Gun, no good, mounted in rear, mostly

indicators.note: the abbreviation is mounted in, set within the other piece
mostly means the word for rear loses its last letter

parts.note: a derriere is a person's behind or rear

explanation.surface: A useless gun has been fixed mostly at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the French-derived word for a backside to DERRIER, ready to have the no-good abbreviation set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol named after its American maker.

clue.text: Broadcasting service covers Open University, in a way

indicators.note: the broadcaster covers, wrapping around the next piece

parts.note: RTE is the Irish state broadcaster
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, a British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A broadcaster provides coverage of a university in some manner.
explanation.walkthrough: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster, and the OU is a British university teaching by distance learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or course taken to reach somewhere.

clue.text: Subject, say, covered in story

indicators.note: the abbreviation is covered in, enclosed by the other word

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A topic is, let's say, treated in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a topic, but it is a feudal subject, a vassal owing loyalty to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a vassal owing feudal service, a subject of a lord.

clue.text: New daily woman

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of daily are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly hired cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DAILY. A daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name.

clue.text: Occasion to apply calcium, initially

indicators.note: initially puts calcium at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
to apply something is to use it

explanation.surface: A reason to put calcium on first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' is a verb here, to bring about, not a noun meaning an event.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion something is to bring it about, the verb sense of cause.

clue.text: Dissolute group, one involved in commercial promotion

indicators.note: the pieces are involved in, taken inside, the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a commercial promotion
a band is a group, often of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild band, one of whose members appears in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolute' is the definition; the advert is just two letters, wrapped round the group and the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wholly given up to vice, so dissolute and depraved.

clue.text: Astoundingly, it's all anyone's done

indicators.note: done in the sense of done over or wrecked tells us the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amazingly, everything anybody did has been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' rearranges the letters of IT'S ALL ANYONE'S, keeping both S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensationally means in a way that causes astonishment or excitement.
